title: Learning control through geometry and optimization
intro: Build from an installed CSL consumer to set representations, controllers, supporting operations, and source-bound environment examples. Every claim names its mathematical scope and evidence role.

groups.label: 4. Conversions, set operations, approximations and optimization

chapters.title: Start with an installed consumer
chapters.summary: Install and validate the package before studying algorithms. The example resolves its public target through the package and checks the returned answer.
chapters.mathematical_input: min -x-2y+7 subject to x>=0, y>=0, x+y<=1
chapters.command:
cmake --preset dev
cmake --build --preset dev --parallel 4
ctest --test-dir build/dev -C Release -R "^installed_public_client$" --output-on-failure
build/dev/installed-consumer/examples-build/registered_lp
chapters.intermediate_geometry: The feasible triangle has vertices (0,0), (1,0), (0,1); the minimizer is (0,1).
chapters.support_limits: The example configures against the installed package and calls the exported CSL::highs_lp target. This native build needs the repository development toolchain and pinned dependencies.

chapters.title: Name coordinates and outcomes
chapters.summary: The requested flow-mass projections are oxidizer (2,100) and fuel (0.6,30). Undo scaling before reordering scaled coordinates. An observed policy path is not the set of all admissible controls. A soft objective target is not a hard target region.
chapters.intermediate_geometry: The requested flow-mass projections are oxidizer (2,100) and fuel (0.6,30). Undo scaling before reordering scaled coordinates.
chapters.support_limits: An observed policy path is not the set of all admissible controls. A soft objective target is not a hard target region.

chapters.title: Use LP membership to remove redundant vertices
chapters.summary: The midpoint is a convex combination of opposite corners. Removing it leaves the unit square unchanged. Membership decisions use the registered numerical LP and specified bounded checks. Resource stops and incomplete outcomes must remain visible.
chapters.mathematical_input: V={(0,0),(1,0),(1,1),(0,1),(0.5,0.5)}. The reducer tests each row against the convex hull of the remaining rows.
chapters.expected_output: Installed hull client: canonical square and completed registered LP receipts passed
chapters.intermediate_geometry: The reducer removes row 4 and retains source rows 0, 1, 2, and 3. Five LP queries complete for the LP membership reducer. The phase-one basis reducer and recursive split/merge path also retain the four square corners.
chapters.support_limits: The result uses numerical HiGHS LP receipts. The client checks completion and retained source indices. It does not certify exact arithmetic, and the client exercises three reducers only; the other inventory entries remain reference-only. First complete the installed-consumer setup in the opening chapter. Its CTest installs the current package and builds the isolated clients with find_package(CSL CONFIG).

chapters.title: Compare source-index hull methods in a 2D operation
chapters.summary: Check every input point, including interior points, edge points, and duplicates. KPABEP/MODIF preserve source order, pivots, epsilon, and stops. QuickHull is a distinct modern comparator. Saved timings do not imply a general speedup.
chapters.mathematical_input: The ordered cloud is [(0,0),(1,0),(1,1),(0,1),(0.5,0),(0,0),(1/3,1/3)]. The affine map is (x,y) ↦ (x+0.25, 0.5x+y−0.5). The one-step sum adds x0=(0.25,0.5) to the same control square.
chapters.expected_output: Both source-index runs return affine-image vertices {(0.25,-0.5),(1.25,0),(1.25,1),(0.25,0.5)} and one-step-sum vertices {(0.25,0.5),(1.25,0.5),(1.25,1.5),(0.25,1.5)}. Each reports checker status=verified. The legacy consumer reports MODIF, KPABEP port and REACH source pairs passed.
chapters.intermediate_geometry: The affine map produces vertical edges at x=0.25 and x=1.25. Its lower-left vertex is below y=0. Adding x0=(0.25,0.5) to the unit control square produces the translated square [0.25,1.25]×[0.5,1.5].
chapters.support_limits: The saved source-index result is a bounded 2D numerical operation with a 5,000 ms and 64-point exact checker. The checker verifies every generated input point is contained by the selected source IDs; it does not prove minimality. BTULSHOR preserves source-order behavior. These outputs are not a performance comparison or historical REACH reproduction. First complete the installed-consumer setup in the opening chapter. Its CTest installs the current package and builds the isolated clients with find_package(CSL CONFIG).

chapters.title: Keep terminal optimization separate from membership
chapters.summary: The feasible triangle has three vertices; this LP selects (0,1). Terminal LP optimization is not a vertex membership decision. Convex terminal objectives use a separate adapter.
chapters.mathematical_input: State x=(x,y) starts at (0,0). Choose (u,v)∈[0,1]² as the terminal state. Require x+y≥1 and minimize x+y.
chapters.expected_output:
profile=strategy-a.nominal-linear-exact-v1
state_dimension=2 control_dimension=2 horizon=1
terminal_constraint=x+y>=1; 0<=x,y<=1
objective=minimize x+y
exact_optimum=1 optimal_face={(x,y): x+y=1, 0<=x,y<=1}
verified_complete_family=true assurance=numerical
chapters.intermediate_geometry: The feasible target is the unit square intersected with x+y≥1. Its minimum-cost face is the segment from (1,0) to (0,1). The executable reports the complete family and optimum 1.
chapters.support_limits: This is the registered nominal linear exact profile in two dimensions and one stage. Its result uses numerical assurance. A generic terminal objective has no complete-family guarantee. Vertex membership and redundancy are different operations. First complete the installed-consumer setup in the opening chapter. Its CTest installs the current package and builds the isolated clients with find_package(CSL CONFIG).

chapters.title: Compare five set representations on one square
chapters.summary: This analytic calculation compares H/V polytopes, zonotopes, parallelotopes, ellipsoids and boxes on one square. Its Python script does not invoke CSL APIs.
chapters.mathematical_input: Q=[-1,1]^2. H rows: ±x<=1, ±y<=1. V corners: (±1,±1). Z center 0, generators e1,e2. Parallelotope A[-1,1]^2 with A=I. E={x:xᵀx<=2}.
chapters.expected_output:
d=(1.0, 0.0); exact_square=1; outer_disk=1.41421
d=(1.0, 1.0); exact_square=2; outer_disk=2
polytope=exact zonotope=exact parallelotope=exact ellipsoid=outer box=exact
Q subset E; E subset [-sqrt(2),sqrt(2)]^2; Q is [-1,1]^2
chapters.intermediate_geometry: At d=(1,0), Q support is 1 and the enclosing disk support is √2. At d=(1,1), both supports equal 2. Q⊂E⊂[-√2,√2]².
chapters.support_limits: The square, zonotope, parallelotope, and box describe the same exact set in this example. The disk is an outer enclosure. No CSL API is called by this script.

chapters.title: Run the installed set approximation consumers
chapters.summary: Installed clients execute the public box, parallelotope, zonotope-reduction, and ellipsoid APIs on declared inputs. The box and parallelotope clients use the same diamond; the two other clients use their own specified sets.
chapters.mathematical_input: The box/parallelotope client encloses a four-vertex diamond. The zonotope client reduces center 0 with generators e1, e2, and (0.5,0.5). The ellipsoidal client checks two outer members for a square.
chapters.expected_output:
Installed box approximation client: diamond is enclosed with bounds 2 on both axes
Installed box/parallelotope client: rotated diamond bounds passed
Installed zonotope client: independently admitted axis cover passed
Installed ellipsoidal client: two reviewed outer members passed
chapters.intermediate_geometry: Both the box and rotated parallelotope use the diamond with vertices (0,2),(2,0),(0,-2),(-2,0). The axis-aligned box is [-2,2]². The rotated parallelotope uses directions (1,1) and (1,-1) with bounds 2. The zonotope cover uses generators (1.5,0) and (0,1.5). The ellipsoid client checks two separately reviewed outer members.
chapters.support_limits: These are three separate numerical consumer examples, not interchangeable representations of one exact result. The zonotope output is an outer cover. The ellipsoid result is an outer family. Each result has the assurance stated by its client. First complete the installed-consumer setup in the opening chapter. Its CTest installs the current package and builds the isolated clients with find_package(CSL CONFIG).

chapters.title: Read a closed-loop policy trace
chapters.summary: Separate predicted stage coordinates from observed execution state and label the observation update. A deterministic replay is one trajectory. It is not full forward reachability or a nonlinear enclosure.
chapters.mathematical_input: Discrete plant x[k+1]=x[k]+u[k]. At each of two updates, observe x[k], choose u[k]=1-x[k], predict one stage, apply the action, and observe the new state.
chapters.expected_output:
update=0 observation=0 action=1 prediction_end=1 plant_state=1
update=1 observation=1 action=0 prediction_end=1 plant_state=1
chapters.intermediate_geometry: At each update, the one-stage prediction endpoint matches the observed plant state. The trace is one policy-conditioned path in a scalar state coordinate.
chapters.support_limits: This dependency-free discrete example illustrates observation and action timing. It does not invoke a CSL controller or establish full reachability, feasibility for other states, or an enclosure.

chapters.title: Run finite feedback and minimax consumers
chapters.summary: Two installed clients execute finite feedback and finite causal minimax ports on small declared action tables.
chapters.mathematical_input: The finite-feedback client registers a winning action for a bounded finite state/action game. The causal-minimax client supplies a finite terminal-choice table and a finite action table.
chapters.expected_output:
Installed finite feedback client: registered winning action passed
Installed causal minimax client: terminal choice and action passed
chapters.intermediate_geometry: The feedback client selects a registered winning action. The causal-minimax client compares the finite terminal choices and returns the selected action.
chapters.support_limits: These clients establish finite-table behavior only. They do not model the three nonlinear capstones or establish full-state reachable-set guarantees. The native environment substitutions remain pending issue #943. First complete the installed-consumer setup in the opening chapter. Its CTest installs the current package and builds the isolated clients with find_package(CSL CONFIG).

chapters.title: Compose reachability, recovery, and MPC
chapters.summary: The complete optimal joint family is (x0,x1,x2,u0,u1)=(0,s,1,s,1-s), 0<=s<=1. The exact-family verifier applies only to its registered profiles. Generic Strategy A/B paths are numerical candidates. Local NLP MPC makes no global optimum claim.
chapters.mathematical_input: The discrete two-stage integrator is x1=x0+u0, x2=x1+u1 with x0=0, ui∈[0,1], and cost (x2−1)². The exact complete optimal family is (x0,x1,x2,u0,u1)=(0,s,1,s,1−s), 0≤s≤1.
chapters.command:
ctest --test-dir build/dev -C Release -R "^installed_public_client$" --output-on-failure
build/dev/installed-consumer/examples-build/registered_synthesis_comparison examples/scenarios/two-stage-integrator.json | python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print("schema="+d["schema"]); [print(r["strategy"]+" termination="+r["termination"]+" outcome="+r["outcome"]+" witnesses="+str(len(r["witnesses"]))+" objective="+str(r["witnesses"][0]["recomputed_objective"])) for r in d["results"]]'
chapters.expected_output:
schema=csl.example.synthesis-comparison/1
csl.synthesis.reach-back termination=completed outcome=optimal witnesses=2 objective=0
csl.synthesis.strategy-b termination=completed outcome=optimal witnesses=2 objective=0
chapters.intermediate_geometry: Both strategies return the two endpoint histories (u0,u1)=(0,1) and (1,0). Each history reaches x2=1 and has recomputed objective 0. The verifier marks optimality and completeness unsupported for these numerical candidates.
chapters.support_limits: This finite exact integrator comparison is distinct from nonlinear MPC and from a global optimality proof for generic Strategy A/B runs. The family payload is unavailable, so the consumer reports two witnesses only. First complete the installed-consumer setup in the opening chapter. Its CTest installs the current package and builds the isolated clients with find_package(CSL CONFIG).

chapters.title: Convert, map, sum, intersect, and project sets
chapters.group_label: 4. Conversions, set operations, approximations and optimization
chapters.summary: The affine image is [1,3]×[0,1]. Adding R gives [0,4]×[0,1]; projection gives [0,4]. A projected overlap does not prove a full-state intersection. Operations keep their documented representation and numerical limits.
chapters.mathematical_input: Convert H={x∈R²: 0≤x≤1} to V and a unit-square V set back to H. Affine sum: [0,1]+[0,1]. H intersection: A={x:x≤1}, B={x:-x≤0}. Predecessor: x+=x+u, u∈[-1,1], target {2}.
chapters.expected_output:
Installed Qhull conversion client: H-to-V square vertices passed
Installed Qhull conversion client: V-to-H square inequalities passed
Installed affine/sum client: selected LP and hull providers produced a numerical set result
Installed polyhedral client: public H intersection passed
Installed predecessor client: existential integrator interval and unestablished support passed
chapters.intermediate_geometry: H-to-V returns the four unit-square corners. V-to-H returns the four unit-square bounds. The interval sum is [0,2]. The H intersection is [0,1] with two rows. The existential predecessor is [1,3]; the consumer accepts 1 and 3 but rejects 0.875 and 3.125.
chapters.support_limits: Qhull conversion and affine sums use numerical providers and bounded client inputs. The predecessor has unestablished support assurance. The projection demonstrates an existential predecessor for one scalar integrator, not a general full-state intersection. Projected overlap does not prove full-state intersection. First complete the installed-consumer setup in the opening chapter. Its CTest installs the current package and builds the isolated clients with find_package(CSL CONFIG).

chapters.title: Select the optimization role you need
chapters.group_label: 4. Conversions, set operations, approximations and optimization
chapters.summary: An LP returns one optimizer; a membership query returns a predicate; finite minimax is scoped to its finite table. HiGHS is optional. Numerical solver output is not a certificate unless a separate verifier says so.
chapters.mathematical_input: The installed convex client sends a convex objective through the public HiGHS adapter and checks the original objective and KKT residuals.
chapters.expected_output: Installed convex client: original norm, squared provenance and numerical KKT passed
chapters.intermediate_geometry: The client retains a numerical solution and checks its objective provenance and KKT conditions. It is not the vertex-membership query, which uses the LP port.
chapters.support_limits: The HiGHS adapter is optional and must be enabled in the installed package. KKT checks establish numerical evidence, not a formal exact certificate. First complete the installed-consumer setup in the opening chapter. Its CTest installs the current package and builds the isolated clients with find_package(CSL CONFIG).
